## intake_stamp

One stamp attempt of one issue version: the intake step read the issue body and the loop applied (or dropped) what the stamp answered. Count one per (issue, version, attempt).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (issue, version, attempt)

### intake_stamp v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The hash of the issue body the stamp read. |
| `mode` | enum | required | no | one of "run", "dry" | yes | run: the stamp was applied. dry: a dry run. The loop writes only run; dry exists so the type can name a dry run. |
| `outcome` | enum | required | no | one of "ok", "failed", "dropped" | yes | ok: the stamp was applied. failed: the stamp step did not produce an answer. dropped: the answer broke the contract. |
| `area` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The area the stamp named, or null when there is none. |
| `needs_owner` | boolean | required | yes |  | yes | Whether the stamp says the issue needs the owner, or null when there is no answer. |
| `reason` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The one-line needs_owner reason, or null. On a run that failed without an answer (outcome failed), why it ended: timeout, lost, spawn-failed or the read or answer problem. |
| `touches` | array of string | required | no |  | yes | The top-level paths the stamp says the issue touches. |
| `dropped` | array of string | required | no |  | yes | The answer fields the contract dropped. |
| `labels_set` | array of string | required | no |  | yes | The labels the loop added. |
| `labels_kept` | array of string | required | no |  | yes | The labels the loop left alone because the owner had changed them. |
| `model` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The model alias that stamped. |
| `input_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The input tokens of an ended run's agent transcript and every agent nested under it, once per request (loop_entry: an agent step; intake_stamp: the stamp run); null while running, for other kinds and when the transcript could not be read. |
| `output_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The output tokens of an ended run, counted as input_tokens; null otherwise. |
| `cache_read_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The cache-read input tokens of an ended run, counted as input_tokens; null otherwise. |
| `cache_creation_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The cache-creation input tokens of an ended run, counted as input_tokens; null otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "version": "3f2a9c1d",
  "mode": "run",
  "outcome": "ok",
  "area": "factory",
  "needs_owner": false,
  "reason": null,
  "touches": [
    "plugins",
    "docs"
  ],
  "dropped": [],
  "labels_set": [
    "area:factory"
  ],
  "labels_kept": [],
  "model": "sonnet",
  "input_tokens": 1840,
  "output_tokens": 212,
  "cache_read_tokens": 9600,
  "cache_creation_tokens": 410
}
```

## intervention

Someone had to step in where the plan did not foresee it: a person (an owner op, a push, a hand merge, a rescue), the loop's judge (the main conversation, running a control op through the control tool) or the loop with unplanned judgement or recovery (a triage, an unknown step, a park, a guard refusal). Written by the loop, and by hand for a rescue the loop cannot see. Not a stage and not progress. The issue is null for a fleet-level one (a restart, a settings edit). Count one per (issue, cause, fact); each row with a null fact counts. A ci-rerun row carrying flaky records the re-run's result as a second row for the same fact, so it still counts once as an intervention under that key.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): optional
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (issue, cause, fact)

### intervention v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `who` | enum | required | no | one of "person", "loop", "judge" | yes | person: a person did something; loop: the loop had to judge or recover; judge: the loop's judge (the main conversation) ran a control op through the control tool. |
| `cause` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z0-9-]+)?$` | yes | What happened, as a code of v2 SPEC 7.2: for example op:resume, push, hand-merge, rescue, restart, config-file, triage, park, unknown:timeout, free:load, fix:ci or guard:write. An open list: handle a code you do not know. |
| `life` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | The issue's life it happened in, as in transition; null when none applies. |
| `fact` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The key of the fact it records, so it is logged and counted once; null for a hand-recorded rescue. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The pull request involved, when there is one. |
| `flaky` | boolean | optional | yes |  | yes | On a ci-rerun row recording the re-run's result: true when the re-run passed on the same head as the failure; false when it failed again. Null otherwise. |
| `failed_tests` | array of string | optional | yes | maxItems 20; items: maxLength 200 | yes | The names of the tests that failed in the CI run. Null when none were recorded. |
| `failed_jobs` | array of string | optional | yes | maxItems 20; items: maxLength 200 | yes | The names of the CI jobs that failed. Null when none were recorded. |
| `head` | string | optional | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The commit the CI run was on, when known. |
| `detail` | string | required | no |  |  | One line for people saying what happened; empty when none was given. Never parse it. |

Example:

```json
{
  "who": "person",
  "cause": "op:drop",
  "life": null,
  "fact": "op:drop/i91/mvb4ci14",
  "pr": null,
  "detail": "drop 91"
}
```

## loop_entry

Loop bookkeeping that most consumers can ignore: one piece of the loop's own work (an agent step, a tell to the owner, or a task) changed status. Written by the loop's ledger. Never a stage or progress; it shows the device is at work, and the loop rebuilds its ledger's tells and tasks from it after a lost store.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): optional
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### loop_entry v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | required | no | one of "agent-step", "tell", "task" | yes | agent-step: an agent ran one step of an issue; tell: a message to the owner; task: a wake of the loop's model outside a planned step. |
| `key` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The ledger key: the work's identity across retries, for example i92/ltn0brb/review/0821e6a/r2/a1. |
| `status` | enum | required | no | one of "running", "done", "failed", "timed-out", "lost" | yes | The status it changed to. |
| `attempts` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Attempts of this key so far. |
| `class` | enum | required | no | one of "free", "owner", "drive", "develop", "start" | yes | The planner's class for the work. |
| `rule` | string | required | no | minLength 1 |  | The planner rule that planned it, for example S2 or S3. |
| `started_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When this attempt started. |
| `ended_at` | string | required | yes | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When it ended; null while running. |
| `agent_id` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The agent's id, for an agent step; null otherwise. |
| `wake` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The wake's name, for a tell or task, for example parked; null otherwise. |
| `decision` | string | optional | yes |  | yes | A wake's decision, for example hold or done; null when the wake made none. |
| `decision_reason` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 200 |  | Why the wake decided as it did; null when it made no decision. |
| `database` | string | optional | yes |  |  | A schema migrate (task:migrate:<to_version>, wake migrate, written by factory-db-migrate at start-up): the factory database that was migrated. |
| `from_version` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 |  | A schema migrate: the schema version before it; null when unknown (the migrate failed before it was read). |
| `to_version` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 |  | A schema migrate: the highest migration number the image ships. |
| `duration_ms` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 |  | A schema migrate: how long it took, in milliseconds. |
| `outcome` | enum | optional | yes | one of "migrated", "current", "failed", "timed-out", null |  | A schema migrate: migrated (versions applied), current (nothing to apply), failed or timed-out. |
| `error` | string | optional | yes |  |  | A schema migrate: the bootstrap's last error line, at most 300 characters; null when it succeeded. |
| `flake_test` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 512 | yes | A flake bug tell (wake flake-bug): the exact name of the flaky test; null otherwise. |
| `flakes` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | A flake bug tell: how many flakes of the test the window held when the bug was filed; null otherwise. |
| `window_days` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 1 | yes | A flake bug tell: the flake window in days (the flakeWindowDays setting); null otherwise. |
| `first_flake_at` | string | optional | yes | format date-time | yes | A flake bug tell: when the first flake of the test in the window happened; null otherwise. |
| `filed_issue` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 1 | yes | A flake bug tell: the number of the bug the loop filed (or found); null otherwise. |
| `input_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The input tokens of an ended run's agent transcript and every agent nested under it, once per request (loop_entry: an agent step; intake_stamp: the stamp run); null while running, for other kinds and when the transcript could not be read. |
| `output_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The output tokens of an ended run, counted as input_tokens; null otherwise. |
| `cache_read_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The cache-read input tokens of an ended run, counted as input_tokens; null otherwise. |
| `cache_creation_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The cache-creation input tokens of an ended run, counted as input_tokens; null otherwise. |
| `model` | string | optional | yes |  | yes | An ended agent step: the full id of the model the step's own agent ran on (for example claude-opus-5-5), the one of most turns; null otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "kind": "agent-step",
  "key": "i92/ltn0brb/review/0821e6a/r2/a1",
  "status": "done",
  "attempts": 1,
  "class": "drive",
  "rule": "S2",
  "started_at": "2026-10-16T15:59:42.324Z",
  "ended_at": "2026-10-16T16:00:11.254Z",
  "agent_id": "a20142b8cd21d3b2b",
  "wake": null
}
```

## loop_passes

Loop bookkeeping that most consumers can ignore: a summary of one UTC minute of the loop's passes (how many ended, how long they took, how many acted or threw), written once a minute while the loop runs. It shows the loop's pace and settings, never a stage or progress. Written by the loop's pass book.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### loop_passes v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | The start of the UTC minute summed up, inclusive. |
| `to_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | The end of that minute, exclusive: one minute after from_at. |
| `passes` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Passes that ended in the minute. 0 when none did; then every duration below is null. |
| `acting` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Of those passes, how many acted (did something rather than finding nothing to do). |
| `errors` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Of those passes, how many threw. |
| `mean_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean duration of the passes, in milliseconds, rounded; null when there was none. |
| `p50_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The median duration (nearest rank), in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `p90_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The 90th percentile duration (nearest rank), in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `max_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The longest duration, in milliseconds; null when there was no pass. |
| `acting_mean_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean duration of the acting passes, in milliseconds, rounded; null when none acted. |
| `idle_mean_ms` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean duration of the passes that did not act, in milliseconds, rounded; null when every pass acted or there was none. |
| `mode` | enum | required | no | one of "off", "observe", "act" | yes | The loop's mode: off, observe (plans, does not act) or act. |
| `planner` | enum | required | no | one of "v1", "v2" | yes | Which planner the loop ran. |
| `pass_every_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The loop's configured time between passes, in milliseconds. |
| `observe_mean_ms` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean wall time of the minute's passes' observe call, in milliseconds, rounded. Null means no pass in the minute had a measure; older loops leave the field out. |
| `observe_commands_mean_ms` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean time the passes' observe call had at least one read in flight, in milliseconds, rounded. Null means no pass in the minute had a measure; older loops leave the field out. |
| `observe_in_process_mean_ms` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The mean in-process time of the passes' observe call, in milliseconds, rounded. Null means no pass in the minute had a measure; older loops leave the field out. |
| `observe_in_process_max_ms` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The longest in-process time of any pass's observe call, in milliseconds. Null means no pass in the minute had a measure; older loops leave the field out. |
| `input_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The orchestrator (the loop's own main session) input tokens of the requests first found in its transcript since the previous minute's read, once per requestId; step agents are excluded (they are on loop_entry). Null when the minute had no baseline (the first read in this process or of a new session), when the transcript could not be found or read, or when the runtime knows no config dir. Older loops leave the field out. |
| `output_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The orchestrator (the loop's own main session) output tokens of the requests first found in its transcript since the previous minute's read, once per requestId; step agents are excluded (they are on loop_entry). Null when the minute had no baseline (the first read in this process or of a new session), when the transcript could not be found or read, or when the runtime knows no config dir. Older loops leave the field out. |
| `cache_read_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The orchestrator (the loop's own main session) cache-read tokens of the requests first found in its transcript since the previous minute's read, once per requestId; step agents are excluded (they are on loop_entry). Null when the minute had no baseline (the first read in this process or of a new session), when the transcript could not be found or read, or when the runtime knows no config dir. Older loops leave the field out. |
| `cache_creation_tokens` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The orchestrator (the loop's own main session) cache-write tokens of the requests first found in its transcript since the previous minute's read, once per requestId; step agents are excluded (they are on loop_entry). Null when the minute had no baseline (the first read in this process or of a new session), when the transcript could not be found or read, or when the runtime knows no config dir. Older loops leave the field out. |

Example:

```json
{
  "from_at": "2026-10-17T00:46:00.000Z",
  "to_at": "2026-10-17T00:47:00.000Z",
  "passes": 5,
  "acting": 5,
  "errors": 0,
  "mean_ms": 9457,
  "p50_ms": 6384,
  "p90_ms": 24804,
  "max_ms": 24804,
  "acting_mean_ms": 9457,
  "idle_mean_ms": null,
  "mode": "act",
  "planner": "v2",
  "pass_every_ms": 10000
}
```

## main_state

One change in the state of a repo's default branch as the loop read it: its head, the newest completed run of each workflow, whether main is green and the newest deployment of each environment. Written only when something changed since the last event of the repo. The factory loop writes it (rule M1), reading the branch every mainEveryMs. Count one per (repo, device, observed_at). The arrays workflows, workflow_ids, run_ids, run_attempts, run_heads, run_events, conclusions and running line up index by index; so do deploy_environments, deploy_ids and deploy_states.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (repo, device, observed_at)

### main_state v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `observed_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the loop read the state of the branch: UTC, ISO 8601, exactly three millisecond digits. |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The default branch name. |
| `head` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` | yes | The commit the branch pointed at when read. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The pull request the head commit came from; null when it is not known or the commit did not come from a pull request. |
| `workflows` | array of string | required | no | items: minLength 1 |  | The names of the repo's workflows, one per index. Every array of workflow facts lines up with this one index by index. |
| `workflow_ids` | array of integer | required | no |  |  | The workflow ids, in the order of workflows. |
| `run_ids` | array of integer | required | no |  |  | The id of the newest completed run of each workflow on the branch; null when it has none. |
| `run_attempts` | array of integer | required | no |  |  | The attempt number of that run; null when it has none. |
| `run_heads` | array of string | required | no |  |  | The commit that run ran on; null when it has none. |
| `run_events` | array of string | required | no |  |  | What started that run, such as push, schedule or workflow_dispatch; null when it has none. |
| `conclusions` | array of string | required | no |  |  | How that run ended: success, failure, cancelled, skipped, timed_out, neutral, action_required, startup_failure or stale; null when there is no completed run. |
| `running` | array of boolean | required | no |  |  | true when a newer run of that workflow is queued or in progress. |
| `green` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when the newest completed run of every workflow concluded success, skipped or neutral. |
| `deploy_environments` | array of string | required | no | items: minLength 1 |  | The deployment environments of the repo, one per index; empty when the repo has none. deploy_ids and deploy_states line up with this one. |
| `deploy_ids` | array of integer | required | no |  |  | The id of the newest deployment of each environment, in the order of deploy_environments. |
| `deploy_states` | array of string | required | no |  |  | The state of that deployment: success, failure, error, inactive, in_progress, queued or pending; null when none is known. |
| `changed` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z_]+$` | yes | What changed since the last main_state event of the repo: first, head, workflow or deploy. |

Example:

```json
{
  "observed_at": "2026-10-19T08:00:00.123Z",
  "branch": "main",
  "head": "f94eb46adde9adb19a154dc41e32877369596f3b",
  "pr": 141,
  "workflows": [
    "ci"
  ],
  "workflow_ids": [
    1001
  ],
  "run_ids": [
    null
  ],
  "run_attempts": [
    null
  ],
  "run_heads": [
    null
  ],
  "run_events": [
    null
  ],
  "conclusions": [
    null
  ],
  "running": [
    true
  ],
  "green": true,
  "deploy_environments": [],
  "deploy_ids": [],
  "deploy_states": [],
  "changed": "first"
}
```

## merged

A pull request for the issue was merged. Written by callum-flow-merge on the device that merged it, by the loop when it finds a merge that no merged event recorded, or by callum-flow-sweep (actor sweep) when it finds a merge that no event recorded: one on the issue's branch, or a merged pull request to the default branch that no merged event names by pr (logged as a hand merge, recovered, with the issue only when the pull request's author is trusted and it closes one). Ends the claim; the end point of lead time and throughput. Count one per pr and head. A reader places and ages a merge by coalesce(merged_at, ts), because ts is when the event was written, which for a recovered merge is later than the merge; merged.title is a fallback to the ready/claimed title.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): optional
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: pr and head

### merged v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The merged pull request; null when the loop found a merge it cannot name. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The merged branch, when known. |
| `head` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The commit that was merged, when known. |
| `by` | enum | required | no | one of "factory", "hand" | yes | factory: the factory merged it; hand: a person merged it outside the factory. |
| `recovered` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when the loop or the sweep logged it afterwards because no merged event was recorded at the merge. |
| `files` | array of string | optional | yes | items: minLength 1 | yes | The repo-relative paths the merged pull request changed, taken from GitHub's pull request files at merge time. Complete up to GitHub's own cap on that list. null when unknown, for example a pr of null or a size that could not be read. A recovered merge can carry it, read when the event was logged. |
| `file_lines` | array of object | optional | yes |  | yes | The pull request's per-file line counts ({path, additions, deletions}) from GitHub's pull request files at merge time, in the same order as files and up to the same cap. An entry whose counts are not non-negative integers is left out here but still counts in files. null when unknown. |
| `additions` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The pull request's total lines added, as GitHub reports them at merge time. null when unknown. |
| `deletions` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The pull request's total lines deleted, as GitHub reports them at merge time. null when unknown. |
| `merged_at` | string | optional | yes | format date-time | yes | When GitHub says the pull request merged (its mergedAt, copied as given). null when unknown. |
| `train` | enum | optional | yes | one of "rode", "dropped", null | yes | Whether the merge rode the merge train: rode when callum-flow-merge was given --tested-tree (CI had passed the tree the merge produced), dropped when it was given --train-dropped (a built train was given up, train_reason says why), null otherwise. |
| `train_reason` | enum | optional | yes | one of "head-moved", "outside-merge", "conflict", "train-red", "left-queue", "tree-mismatch", "refused", null | yes | Why a built train was dropped, set only when train is dropped; null otherwise. |
| `tested_tree` | string | optional | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` | yes | The tree sha CI passed on the train branch, set only when train is rode; null otherwise. |
| `tree_matched` | boolean | optional | yes |  | yes | When train is rode: whether the merge commit's tree equals tested_tree (false means main landed on a tree CI did not pass). null when there was no train or the merge commit's tree could not be read. |
| `title` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 256 | yes | The closed issue's title when the event has an issue and its author is trusted, otherwise the pull request's title when its author is trusted, clipped to 256 characters. null when neither was read. |

Example:

```json
{
  "pr": 141,
  "branch": "issue-85-usage-panel",
  "head": "f94eb46adde9adb19a154dc41e32877369596f3b",
  "by": "factory",
  "recovered": false
}
```

## milestone_state

The state of a repo's release milestone (Next): how much is closed and open, how long the oldest closed work has waited, the last tag, the release size expected and whether the judge is holding the release. Written only when one of these values changes.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### milestone_state v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `milestone_closed` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Closed issues in the milestone. |
| `milestone_open` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Open issues in the milestone. |
| `oldest_closed_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time |  | When the oldest closed issue in the milestone closed; null when none is closed. |
| `last_tag` | string | required | yes |  |  | The newest release tag; null when the repo has none. |
| `oldest_unreleased_merge_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time |  | When the oldest merged pull request not yet in a release merged; null when none. |
| `expected` | enum | required | yes | one of "patch", "minor", "major", null |  | The size of the release the unreleased work calls for; null when undecided. |
| `holding` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when the newest release task for this milestone ended in hold and no release followed. |
| `hold_reason` | string | required | yes | maxLength 200 |  | Why the judge held; null when not holding. |

Example:

```json
{
  "milestone_closed": 3,
  "milestone_open": 1,
  "oldest_closed_at": "2026-10-17T10:00:00Z",
  "last_tag": "v0.61.0",
  "oldest_unreleased_merge_at": "2026-10-17T09:55:12Z",
  "expected": "minor",
  "holding": true,
  "hold_reason": "an open issue changes the same schema"
}
```

## prompt_denied

An agent's tool use needed a permission nobody could grant, and the companion denied it (an unattended session cannot answer a prompt). Written by the loop's companion. Not a stage and not progress. The companion never retries the write, so count one per event_id.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: event_id

### prompt_denied v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `life` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | Which life of the issue the prompt came in; null when unknown. |
| `seq` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The record's sequence in this life; null when unknown. |
| `step` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The step the agent was running, for example build; null when unknown. |
| `attempt` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The attempt of that step; null when unknown. |
| `agent_id` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The agent's id; null when the prompt came from no sub-agent. |
| `agent_type` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The agent's type, for example Explore or general-purpose; null when unknown. |
| `tool_name` | string | required | yes |  | yes | Claude Code's tool the prompt was for, for example Bash; null when unknown. |
| `tool_input` | string | required | yes | maxLength 2000 | yes | What the tool was asked to do: the Bash command, else the input as JSON, cut at 2000 characters; null when unknown. |
| `ask_reason` | string | required | yes | maxLength 500 |  | Claude Code's reason, rule and decider for asking, cut at 500 characters; null when unknown. |
| `slot` | string | required | yes |  |  | The writer's slot (worktree path) the prompt came from; null when unknown. |
| `session` | string | required | yes |  |  | The Claude Code session id; null when unknown. |
| `transcript` | string | required | yes |  |  | The path of the session's transcript; null when unknown. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The issue's branch; null when unknown. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The issue's PR number; null when it has none yet. |

Example:

```json
{
  "life": "ltn0brb",
  "seq": 12,
  "step": "build",
  "attempt": 1,
  "agent_id": "a20142b8cd21d3b2b",
  "agent_type": "general-purpose",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": "git push origin main",
  "ask_reason": "permission rule: ask Bash(git push:*), decided by the user's settings",
  "slot": "/work/slots/3/repo",
  "session": "01MR3Be83yxy3baM8zGwY7jA",
  "transcript": "/home/user/.claude/projects/repo/01MR3Be83yxy3baM8zGwY7jA.jsonl",
  "branch": "issue-92",
  "pr": 101
}
```

## prompt_waiting

An agent stopped on a permission prompt and is waiting for an answer nobody gives (the companion saw Claude Code's notification). Written by the loop's companion. Not a stage and not progress. The companion never retries the write, so count one per event_id.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: event_id

### prompt_waiting v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `life` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | Which life of the issue the prompt came in; null when unknown. |
| `seq` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The record's sequence in this life; null when unknown. |
| `step` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The step the agent was running, for example build; null when unknown. |
| `attempt` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The attempt of that step; null when unknown. |
| `agent_id` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The agent's id; null when the prompt came from no sub-agent. |
| `agent_type` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The agent's type, for example Explore or general-purpose; null when unknown. |
| `tool_name` | string | required | yes |  | yes | Always null: the notification names no tool. |
| `tool_input` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The notification's message, which says what the agent waits for, cut at 2000 characters; null when unknown. |
| `slot` | string | required | yes |  |  | The writer's slot (worktree path) the prompt came from; null when unknown. |
| `session` | string | required | yes |  |  | The Claude Code session id; null when unknown. |
| `transcript` | string | required | yes |  |  | The path of the session's transcript; null when unknown. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The issue's branch; null when unknown. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The issue's PR number; null when it has none yet. |

Example:

```json
{
  "life": "ltn0brb",
  "seq": 12,
  "step": "build",
  "attempt": 1,
  "agent_id": null,
  "agent_type": null,
  "tool_name": null,
  "tool_input": "Claude needs your permission to use Bash",
  "slot": "/work/slots/3/repo",
  "session": "01MR3Be83yxy3baM8zGwY7jA",
  "transcript": "/home/user/.claude/projects/repo/01MR3Be83yxy3baM8zGwY7jA.jsonl",
  "branch": "issue-92",
  "pr": null
}
```

## queue_snapshot

The loop's view of the claim queue at the end of one claim pass: the candidates in rank order with each one's score, its factors and whether the claim rule would take it (and if not, why not), the claims left under the in-flight cap and the owner's controls in force. Written when the view changes and as a heartbeat when it does not, so the newest snapshot of a repo shows how fresh the loop's view is. A claim pass's immediate write is reason changed. Written by the factory loop.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### queue_snapshot v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `taken_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the pass that produced the view ended. |
| `reason` | enum | required | no | one of "changed", "heartbeat" | yes | Why the snapshot was written: changed (the view differs from the last write; a claim pass's immediate write is always this) or heartbeat (unchanged, written to show the loop is alive). |
| `considered` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many candidates the claim rule considered this pass: the whole list, before the cap on candidates below. |
| `candidates` | array of object | required | no | maxItems 50 | yes | The first 50 candidates in rank order. why is null exactly when claimable is true. |
| `rest` | array of object | required | no |  | yes | The candidates past the first 50, counted by why code (null = claimable). Empty when there are 50 or fewer. |
| `free_slots` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | Claims left under maxInFlightIssues this pass; null when the cap is unset. |
| `owner_priority` | array of integer | required | no |  | yes | The owner's priority list in force; empty when off. |
| `owner_only` | array of integer | required | no |  | yes | The owner's 'only' list in force; empty when off. |
| `owner_serial` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | Whether the owner's 'one at a time' control is on. |
| `owner_new_off` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | Whether the owner's 'no new work' control is on. |
| `folded` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many queue changes since the previous write this write folds in; 0 for a heartbeat with no change. |

Example:

```json
{
  "taken_at": "2026-10-20T17:35:00.000Z",
  "reason": "changed",
  "considered": 3,
  "candidates": [
    {
      "issue": 1148,
      "rank": 1,
      "score": 42,
      "factors": [
        {
          "name": "bug",
          "points": 25
        },
        {
          "name": "waiting",
          "points": 17
        }
      ],
      "claimable": true,
      "why": null
    },
    {
      "issue": 1147,
      "rank": 2,
      "score": 10,
      "factors": [
        {
          "name": "waiting",
          "points": 10
        }
      ],
      "claimable": false,
      "why": "blocked"
    },
    {
      "issue": 1160,
      "rank": 3,
      "score": null,
      "factors": null,
      "claimable": false,
      "why": "unknown"
    }
  ],
  "rest": [],
  "free_slots": 2,
  "owner_priority": [],
  "owner_only": [],
  "owner_serial": false,
  "owner_new_off": false,
  "folded": 3
}
```

## ready

The issue was seen with the ready label: it is in the factory's queue. Written by queue-watch, which the loop runs each pass, once per issue newly seen. Starts the clock for lead time. Also carries the issue's title, labels and parent as the queue listing showed them.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### ready v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 256 | yes | The issue's title as the producer read it, clipped to 256 characters; null when it was not read. An issue's newest title is the title of its newest ready or claimed event by ts that has a non-null title. |
| `labels` | array of string | optional | yes |  | yes | The issue's label names in GitHub's order, as the producer read them: on ready, the labels of the queue listing; on claimed, the labels after the claim (the ready label the claim removed is left out). Null when they were not read. |
| `parent` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The parent issue's number when the parent is in the same repo. Null when there is no parent, when the parent is in another repo, or when it was not read. |

Example:

```json
{}
```

## released

A release tag was cut: the tag, the tag before it, the commit it points at, the pull requests and issues it carried and the headlines of its release notes. Count it once by (repo, tag): the same release can be seen by more than one device.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### released v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tag` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The release tag, for example v0.61.0. |
| `previous_tag` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The release tag before this one; null for a first release. |
| `commit` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The sha the tag points at. |
| `released_at` | string | required | no | format date-time |  | The tag commit's time, copied as given. |
| `prs` | array of integer | required | no |  | yes | The pull requests the release carried. |
| `issues` | array of integer | required | no |  | yes | Every issue those pull requests link, closing or not. |
| `issues_closed` | array of integer | required | no |  | yes | The issues those pull requests close. |
| `headlines` | array of string | required | no | items: maxLength 200 | yes | The release notes' headlines, one per entry. |
| `source` | enum | required | no | one of "loop", "workflow", "manual" |  | Who cut the release: the loop, the release workflow, or a person by hand. |

Example:

```json
{
  "tag": "v0.61.0",
  "previous_tag": "v0.60.0",
  "commit": "e691458",
  "released_at": "2026-10-18T21:04:11Z",
  "prs": [
    1050,
    1052
  ],
  "issues": [
    1009,
    1010
  ],
  "issues_closed": [
    1010
  ],
  "headlines": [
    "Test the 10-minor schema window against each tag's writers and readers"
  ],
  "source": "loop"
}
```

## requeued

The issue's claim was given back and the issue is in the queue again (ready label on), for any device to take. Written by callum-flow-sweep when a lease ran out, and by the loop's reconcile or factory-reconcile when it released a claim with no live work behind it and put the issue back in the queue. Ends the claim. A reconcile release that takes the issue out of the factory is abandoned instead.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### requeued v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | enum | required | no | one of "lease-expired", "reconcile" | yes | Why: lease-expired (no renewal in time) or reconcile (reconcile found no live work behind the claim and requeued it). |
| `stage` | string | required | yes |  |  | reconcile: the v2 state (queued, designing, building, reviewing, fixing, parked and so on) callum-flow-factory-state showed the issue in; rows written before the tool switch hold the old stage words (implementing, in pipeline, ready to merge); null otherwise. |
| `lives` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | reconcile: the released life's number among the issue's lives, when known; null otherwise. |
| `branch` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The released work's branch, when known. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The released work's open pull request, when there is one. |
| `detail` | string | required | yes |  |  | reconcile: what was checked, one line for people; never parse it. null otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "reason": "lease-expired",
  "stage": null,
  "lives": null,
  "branch": null,
  "pr": null,
  "detail": null
}
```

## reviewed

One review of the issue's pull request finished. Written by the loop from the reviewer's answer. Not a stage and not progress. A retried write can repeat it: count one per answer_path.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: answer_path

### reviewed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The reviewed branch. |
| `pr` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The reviewed pull request. |
| `head` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The commit that was reviewed. |
| `verdict` | enum | required | no | one of "approve", "changes", "unknown" | yes | approve, changes (findings to fix), or unknown (no valid answer). |
| `round` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The review round in this life, from 1. |
| `patch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The patch id reviewed: an approval holds for exactly this patch. |
| `errors` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Findings of severity error. |
| `warnings` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 |  | Findings of severity warning. |
| `infos` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 |  | Findings of severity info. |
| `reviewer` | string | required | no | minLength 1 |  | Which reviewer answered, for example adjudicator. |
| `ui_capture` | string | optional | yes | one of "command", "none", "unset", null |  | The repo's UI capture policy the review ran under: command (a capture command is set), none (capture is off, so a missing capture is at most a warning) or unset. Optional: absent or null on a review recorded before the field existed. |
| `answer_path` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The reviewer's answer file on the loop's device. Identifies the review: one event per answer. |

Example:

```json
{
  "branch": "issue-92-tunnel-token",
  "pr": 143,
  "head": "c46dbb8606d93ca2a59c70507a7edfab290a621e",
  "verdict": "changes",
  "round": 1,
  "patch": "c46dbb8606d93ca2a59c70507a7edfab290a621e",
  "errors": 1,
  "warnings": 0,
  "infos": 2,
  "reviewer": "adjudicator",
  "answer_path": "/persist/claude/factory-loop/cbundy__plant-console/answers/i92_ltn0brb_review_c46dbb8_r1_a1.answer.json"
}
```

## settings_changed

One change in a setting the loop runs on: which setting, its old and new value, the layer the new value came from and who changed it. Count one per fact (the once key, such as settings/maxInFlightIssues/mvb4ci14). The loop writes it (rule N1): each acting pass compares its settings snapshot with the one it kept and logs one event for every setting that differs.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: fact (the once key, such as settings/maxInFlightIssues/mvb4ci14)

### settings_changed v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The canonical leaf of the setting, such as maxInFlightIssues, stateTimeoutMs.design or derived.gateConcurrency. |
| `old_value` | any | required | no |  | yes | The value before the change, any JSON; null when it was unset. |
| `new_value` | any | required | no |  | yes | The value after the change, any JSON; null when it is now unset. |
| `layer` | enum | required | yes | one of "default", "repo", "workspace", "plugin", "env", "directive", null | yes | The source of the new value; null for a derived value. |
| `who` | enum | required | no | one of "person", "judge", "repo", "plugin" | yes | Who made the change: a person, the judge (an operation change), the repo (its own config) or a plugin default change. |
| `fact` | string | required | no |  | yes | The once key of the change, such as settings/maxInFlightIssues/mvb4ci14. |
| `detail` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 500 |  | A short note on the change. |

Example:

```json
{
  "key": "maxInFlightIssues",
  "old_value": 3,
  "new_value": 5,
  "layer": "workspace",
  "who": "judge",
  "fact": "settings/maxInFlightIssues/mvb4ci14",
  "detail": "raised after a quiet week"
}
```

## shadow_read

One shadow compare made by a reader that has an old/new source switch: the command read the same keys from the old source and the new central one and counted where the answers differ. Written once per compare, not for an issue. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (repo, device, ts).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (repo, device, ts)

### shadow_read v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reader` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` | yes | Which reader was compared, an open family such as claim-events. |
| `tool` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The command that made the compare, such as callum-flow-sweep. |
| `compared` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many keys were compared. |
| `differences` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many keys whose answers differ, with both sides cut at the settle time. |
| `live_differences` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many keys whose answers differ on everything read, push lag included. |
| `diff_keys` | array of string | required | no | maxItems 50 |  | The keys that differ, at most 50. |
| `old_ok` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | Whether the central read of the old side succeeded. |
| `new_ok` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | Whether the central read of the new side succeeded. |
| `settle_seconds` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The settle time in seconds: both sides are cut this far back so push lag is not counted as a difference. |
| `detail` | string | required | yes | maxLength 500 |  | The first difference as old against new, or null when there is none. |
| `scope_floor` | string | optional | yes |  |  | The writing device's first time in the new store for the repo (ISO, whole seconds), or null when it has none. The compare leaves out of both sides the events of a device older than its floor, history the new store never held. |
| `out_of_scope` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 |  | How many events the floor left out of both sides, or null when the reader does not count them. |

Example:

```json
{
  "reader": "claim-events",
  "tool": "callum-flow-sweep",
  "compared": 42,
  "differences": 0,
  "live_differences": 0,
  "diff_keys": [],
  "old_ok": true,
  "new_ok": true,
  "settle_seconds": 120,
  "detail": null
}
```

## test_weakened

A commit on a merged pull request deleted or weakened a test (removed an assertion, added a skip, .only, --warn-only or || true, or commented an assertion out). Written by callum-flow-merge, one per flagged commit.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### test_weakened v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The merged branch. |
| `pr` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The merged pull request. |
| `head` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The merged head. |
| `commit` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The flagged commit (short sha). |
| `restored` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when a later commit on the branch put the test back. |
| `kinds` | array of string | required | no | minItems 1 |  | What the commit did to the tests, one code each, for example removed-assertion. |
| `files` | array of string | required | no | minItems 1 | yes | The test files it touched, repo-relative. |

Example:

```json
{
  "branch": "issue-72-orchestrator-view",
  "pr": 97,
  "head": "9b1e0c4f2a7d",
  "commit": "3ae20a1",
  "restored": false,
  "kinds": [
    "removed-assertion"
  ],
  "files": [
    "tests/web/orchestrators.test.ts"
  ]
}
```

## transition

The loop's record of the issue changed: it moved to a new state, or its step, attempt or notes changed. Written by the loop on every record change, and again after a re-claim. It carries the whole record, so the loop rebuilds a lost record from the newest one; to_state is the issue's state for the factory tools. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (issue, life, seq).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (issue, life, seq)

### transition v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `life` | string | required | no | pattern `^[0-9a-z]+$` | yes | Which life of the issue: one per pass through the factory, named by when its claim started (seconds, base 36). |
| `seq` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The record's sequence in this life: one more on every transition. |
| `table_row` | string | required | no | pattern `^([A-Z][0-9]+\|recovered)$` | yes | The row of the loop's transition table that fired, for example T9 or U1 (v2 SPEC 4.3); recovered when the loop rebuilt the record after losing the step's outcome, and then via is recovered too. |
| `from_state` | enum | required | yes | one of "queued", "designing", "building", "reviewing", "fixing", "merge-queue", "parked", "waiting", "closed", null | yes | The state before; null for a life's first transition. |
| `to_state` | enum | required | no | one of "queued", "designing", "building", "reviewing", "fixing", "merge-queue", "parked", "waiting", "closed" | yes | The state after: the issue's state from now on. |
| `via` | string | required | no | pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z0-9-]+)?$` | yes | A short code for what moved it, for example approve, fix:review, free:load, unknown:timeout, triage:retry, unreject, reclaim (logged again after a re-claim) or dual-write (logged again when the new log lacked it). An open list: handle a code you do not know. |
| `seq_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When this transition happened. Time transitions by this, not by the envelope ts: a transition logged again after a re-claim keeps its seq_at. |
| `state_since` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the issue entered to_state; earlier than seq_at when the state did not change. |
| `resume_to` | enum | required | yes | one of "queued", "designing", "building", "reviewing", "fixing", "merge-queue", "parked", "waiting", "closed", null | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: when to_state is queued, the state a new claim leads to; when parked, the state unparking leads to; when waiting, the state the loop resumes to once every condition in wait holds; null otherwise. |
| `branch` | string | required | no | minLength 1 | yes | The life's branch, fixed for the life. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The life's pull request; null until there is one. |
| `head` | string | required | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` | yes | The head commit a step last confirmed on origin; null before the first push. |
| `approved_patch` | string | required | yes |  |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: the patch id the reviewer approved; null until an approval. |
| `brief_url` | string | required | yes |  | yes | The URL of the design brief comment; null until the designer posts one. |
| `step` | enum | required | yes | one of "lease", "design", "build", "review", "fix", "queue", "triage", null | yes | The step this seq runs: the state's own step, or triage; null while waiting. |
| `attempt` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | The attempt of that step, from 1. |
| `cut` | boolean | required | no |  |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: true when this attempt already had its one free re-run. |
| `triages` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: triage calls so far in this life. |
| `fixes` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: entries to fixing so far in this life. |
| `round` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | Entries to reviewing so far in this life: the review round. |
| `question` | string | required | yes | maxLength 2000 | yes | parked: the question for the owner; null otherwise. For people; never parse it. |
| `decision` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 2000 | yes | parked: the one-sentence ask of the owner's question, set only when an agent structured the question; null otherwise. Shares the decision column with loop_entry. |
| `context` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 800 | yes | parked: the context of the owner's question, set only when an agent structured the question; null otherwise. |
| `options` | array of object | optional | yes | minItems 2; maxItems 6 | yes | parked: the options of the owner's question, set only when an agent structured the question; null otherwise. |
| `recommended` | enum | optional | yes | one of "A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", null | yes | parked: the key of the recommended option, set only when an agent structured the question; null otherwise. |
| `recommendation` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 200 | yes | parked: the reason for the recommended option, set only when an agent structured the question; null otherwise. |
| `wait` | array of object | optional | yes | minItems 1; maxItems 8 |  | waiting: the conditions the loop re-checks each pass; null otherwise |
| `why` | enum | required | yes | one of "merged", "merged-by-hand", "dropped", "split", "closed-on-github", "claim-lost", "done", null | yes | closed: why the life ended (done: its work had already merged); null otherwise. |
| `notes` | array of string | required | no | maxItems 8; items: maxLength 1000 | yes | Loop state, for the record rebuild: owner, triage and decline notes for this seq's step, oldest first. For people and the step's agent; never parse them. |
| `pr_closed_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: GitHub's closedAt of the newest hand-closed pull request the loop has handled, exactly as GitHub gave it (the loop compares it as text, so it is never reformatted); null when none. |
| `conflicts` | integer | optional | yes | minimum 0 |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: the entries to fixing in this life caused by a conflict or red CI after other merges. Absent (or null) before the loop counted them; absent is read as 0. |
| `env_blocked` | string | optional | yes | maxLength 1000 |  | Loop state, for the record rebuild: the environment-blocker reasons of the previous fix round in this life (one clipped line); null when that round had none. A second fix round with one parks the issue. Absent is read as null. |
| `lives` | integer | required | no | minimum 1 | yes | This life's number among the issue's lives since the count last started; the issue is rejected at the configured maximum. |

Example:

```json
{
  "life": "tn0brb",
  "seq": 6,
  "table_row": "T11",
  "from_state": "fixing",
  "to_state": "reviewing",
  "via": "fix",
  "seq_at": "2026-10-16T15:59:06.252Z",
  "state_since": "2026-10-16T15:59:06.252Z",
  "resume_to": null,
  "branch": "issue-92-tunnel-token",
  "pr": 143,
  "head": "0821e6a3c0f4b1d2e5a6978877665544332211ff",
  "approved_patch": null,
  "brief_url": "https://github.com/cbundy/plant-console/issues/92#issuecomment-6219193862",
  "step": "review",
  "attempt": 1,
  "cut": false,
  "triages": 0,
  "fixes": 1,
  "round": 2,
  "conflicts": 1,
  "question": null,
  "why": null,
  "notes": [],
  "pr_closed_at": null,
  "lives": 1
}
```

## untrusted_stripped

A read of GitHub content dropped text by untrusted authors, or refused an untrusted issue, pull request or comment outright. Written by callum-flow-issue-read. A security trail: the dropped text itself is never logged.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): required
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### untrusted_stripped v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | enum | required | no | one of "issue", "pr", "comment", "comments", "timeline", "list" |  | What was being read: an issue, a pull request or a comment (refused whole), or an issue's comments, its timeline or an issue list (items dropped). |
| `refused` | boolean | required | no |  |  | true: the whole item was refused because its author is untrusted; false: untrusted items were dropped from it. |
| `count` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 |  | How many items were dropped; null when refused. |
| `pr` | integer | required | yes | minimum 1 | yes | The pull request read, when it was one. |

Example:

```json
{
  "source": "timeline",
  "refused": false,
  "count": 2,
  "pr": null
}
```

## usage

A reading of the Claude subscription's usage windows. Written by usage-check, which the loop runs on its schedule. Shows how close the device is to a rate limit.

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: not stated

### usage v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `available` | boolean | required | no |  | yes | true when a reading was had; false when no source gave one (then every reading field is null). A spend reading has available true and null window fields. |
| `five_hour_pct` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | Percent of the five-hour window used, rounded up. |
| `five_hour_resets_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time | yes | When the five-hour window resets. |
| `seven_day_pct` | integer | required | yes | minimum 0 | yes | Percent of the most used seven-day window, rounded up. |
| `seven_day_resets_at` | string | required | yes | format date-time | yes | When that seven-day window resets. |
| `source` | enum | required | yes | one of "oauth", "statusline", "spend", null |  | Where the reading came from; null when unavailable. spend is a spend reading against a budget, which has null window fields. |
| `auth` | enum | optional | yes | one of "subscription", "api-key", null | yes | Which login the reading was taken under. |
| `spend_usd` | number | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | Dollars spent in the current budget period up to the reading. |
| `budget_usd` | number | optional | yes | minimum 0 | yes | The budget for that period, in dollars. |
| `budget_resets_at` | string | optional | yes | format date-time | yes | When the budget period resets. |
| `reasons` | array of string | required | no |  |  | When unavailable: why, one code per source tried, for example statusline:bad-snapshot; empty otherwise. |

Example:

```json
{
  "available": true,
  "five_hour_pct": 21,
  "five_hour_resets_at": "2026-10-16T16:00:00.000Z",
  "seven_day_pct": 4,
  "seven_day_resets_at": "2026-10-23T11:00:00.000Z",
  "source": "oauth",
  "reasons": []
}
```

## wind_down

One stop of a workspace's loop finished winding down: the loop stopped taking new work, waited for the steps that were running (up to a cap), then stopped. Written once per stop, not for an issue. A retried write can repeat it: count one per (repo, device, requested_at).

- Issue field (`x-issue`): none
- Versions: v1 (current)
- Counting key: (repo, device, requested_at)

### wind_down v1

| Field | Type | Required | Nullable | Bounds or values | Column | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requested_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the stop was asked for. With outcome off it equals stopped_at. |
| `stopped_at` | string | required | no | pattern `^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$` | yes | When the loop stopped. With outcome off it equals requested_at. |
| `waited_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How long the stop waited for running steps, in milliseconds; 0 with outcome off. |
| `cap_ms` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | The longest the stop was allowed to wait, in milliseconds. |
| `outcome` | enum | required | no | one of "idle", "cap", "now", "off" | yes | How the wait ended: idle (no step was left running), cap (the wait cap ran out and the rest were cut), now (stopped at once, running steps cut), or off (wind-down is off: no wait). |
| `running_at_request` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many steps were running when the stop was asked for. |
| `running_at_request_keys` | array of string | required | no |  |  | The loop keys of those steps (stepKey i<N>/l<life>/s<seq>/<step>/a<n>, or reviewKey i<N>/l<life>/review/<patch7>/r<round>/a<n>). |
| `cut_at_stop` | integer | required | no | minimum 0 | yes | How many steps were still running, and cut, when the loop stopped. |
| `cut_at_stop_keys` | array of string | required | no |  | yes | The loop keys of the cut steps, in the same form as running_at_request_keys. Lifted as a jsonb column so a cut step can be joined to its re-run. |
| `trigger` | string | required | yes | one of "restart-self", "coder-stop", null | yes | What asked for the stop: restart-self, coder-stop, or null when not known. |

Example:

```json
{
  "requested_at": "2026-10-17T10:00:00.000Z",
  "stopped_at": "2026-10-17T10:04:10.500Z",
  "waited_ms": 250500,
  "cap_ms": 300000,
  "outcome": "idle",
  "running_at_request": 2,
  "running_at_request_keys": [
    "i840/ltn0brb/s6/build/a1",
    "i841/ltn0brc/review/0821e6a/r2/a1"
  ],
  "cut_at_stop": 0,
  "cut_at_stop_keys": [],
  "trigger": "restart-self"
}
```
